data.title: Kospi Closes Marginally Higher On Bargain Hunting
data.description:
The South Korean stock market closed slightly higher on Oct 23 after plunging more than 3% in the previous session, as investors hunted for bargains in major chip stocks amid persistent concerns over investments in the artificial intelligence value chain.

After choppy trading, the Kospi rose 16.53 points, or 0.3%, to end at 5,550.30.

The index opened 2.36% lower, but individual investors, who were net sellers early in the session, turned to net buying.

Overnight, US stocks closed mixed, with losses in major technology shares weighing on the broader market.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.02%, while the S&P 500 fell 1.21% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite shed 2.6%.

Micron Technology plunged 6.26%, while Nvidia and Intel tumbled 4.4% and 8.04%, respectively.

In Seoul, most large-cap shares traded mixed.

Samsung Electronics increased 0.47% to close at 215,500 won, while rival chipmaker SK hynix went up 4.42% to 1.28 million won after opening lower.

Yonhap

data.title: Hong Kong Stocks Rebound 158.69 Points As Tech, EV Shares Lift Hang Seng Above 23,000
data.description:
Hong Kong stocks rebounded on Oct 23, with the Hang Seng Index climbing 158.69 points or 0.69% to close at 23,093.37, driven by bargain hunting in technology, electric vehicle (EV) and semiconductor stocks following a sharp sell-off in the previous session.

The benchmark recovered from an intraday low of 22,803.77 to finish above the 23,000-point mark, after tumbling 3.03% on Oct 22 amid concerns over global technology valuations and geopolitical tensions.

Technology stocks led the recovery, with the Hang Seng Tech Index surging 77.73 points or 2.05% to 3,871.66, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index advanced 67.06 points or 0.87% to 7,756.25.

EV makers were among the strongest performers, with BYD jumping 6.23% and XPeng gaining 5.1%. Battery manufacturer CATL also advanced approximately 5.4%, reflecting renewed buying interest in growth-oriented counters.

The rebound followed several sessions of heavy selling, as investors returned to technology and automotive stocks that had suffered significant declines.

Mainland Chinese equities also strengthened, providing additional support to Hong Kong’s recovery. The Shanghai Composite Index rose 0.89% to 3,690, while the Shenzhen Component Index surged 2.79% to 11,673.

Trading turnover on the Hong Kong market reached HK$249.78 billion.

However, gains remained constrained by concerns over the Middle East conflict and elevated oil prices, which continued to weigh on global risk sentiment.

Brent crude traded around US$114 a barrel amid geopolitical tensions, raising concerns over inflationary pressures and the outlook for global economic growth.

Despite the recovery on Oct 23, the Hang Seng Index ended the week approximately 4.52% lower, reflecting continued volatility and investor caution over technology valuations, corporate earnings and geopolitical developments.

data.title: Singapore Stocks Edge Higher As Property Gains Offset Banking Weakness
data.description:
Singapore shares ended marginally higher on Oct 23, with the Straits Times Index (STI) gaining 7.02 points or 0.13% to 5,422.16, as gains in property-related counters and easing technology-sector selling pressure helped offset declines in banking heavyweights.

The benchmark index recovered from an intraday low of 5,365.33 to finish above its close of 5,415.14 on Oct 22, despite cautious sentiment surrounding global interest rates and technology valuations.

CapitaLand Investment led STI gainers, climbing 3.9% or nine Singapore cents to S$2.40, while Yangzijiang Shipbuilding was the index’s biggest decliner, falling 1.6% or eight cents to S$4.88.

Singapore’s three major banks ended lower, limiting the benchmark’s advance. DBS slipped 0.2% to S$74.44, OCBC declined 0.2% to S$29.00, while UOB shed 0.7% to S$41.59.

Elsewhere, Keppel DC REIT gained 4% after reporting distributable income of S$228 million for the nine months ended September, up from S$195.3 million a year earlier.

Seatrium rose nearly 2% after securing a contract involving conversion and integration works for five powerships for Karpowership.

CapitaLand China Trust also advanced nearly 1%, despite reporting lower gross revenue for the first nine months of the year.

Across the broader market, gainers outnumbered losers 331 to 258, reflecting selective buying interest despite continued weakness in major banking stocks.

Market sentiment was supported by easing selling pressure in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks, although concerns over elevated US Treasury yields and technology-sector valuations continued to weigh on risk appetite.

Investors are now turning their attention to the US Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision scheduled for Oct 28, with uncertainty over the monetary policy outlook likely to remain a key influence on regional equities.

data.title: Wall Street Closes Lower To End Rocky Week
data.description:
Wall Street’s main ​indexes closed lower on Oct 23 even as technology shares steadied somewhat to end a turbulent week for the market-driving artificial intelligence (AI) trade, ‌and investors looked ahead to a busy slate of corporate earnings and a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest-rate policy meeting.

Reuters reported that the Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss a day after the tech-heavy index suffered its biggest one-day drop since June, as concerns flared over financing costs to support heavy AI investment spending. The S&P 500 technology sector posted a 0.35% gain on Oct 23.

Most S&P 500 sectors fell, however, including declines of well over 1% for the consumer staples and consumer discretionary groups as well as the financial sector.

Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies report quarterly results, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, three AI hyperscalers whose ⁠capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16; the S&P 500 lost 39.75 points, or 0.52%, to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 53.52 points, or 0.21%, to 25,955.34.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%. The blue-chip Dow rose 0.4%, its third straight weekly gain.

Telecommunications stocks fell, weighing on the communication services sector, after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier.

Shares of AT&T and T-Mobile both sank nearly 8% while Verizon shed 1.2%. SpaceX shares rose 1.9%. US cell tower operators gained, with Crown Castle up 9% and American Tower up 4%.

The energy sector rose 2.5%, hitting a record high. Brent crude hit its highest level since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

American Express shares fell 3.7%, weighing on the Dow. The company raised its profit forecast as it also announced plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce.

SLB shares rose 7% after the oilfield services provider beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit.

Data from the University of Michigan showed US consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October, as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households’ views of the economy.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with robust corporate profit growth underpinning gains for major equity indexes this year. companies are on track to have increased earnings by more than 32% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.

The Fed is expected to keep interest rates steady when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, but investors will be eager for clues about whether the US central bank will hike rates at its December meeting. Wall Street is also increasingly focused on the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.72-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. On the Nasdaq, declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.57-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 18 new 52-week highs and 8 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 74 new highs and 334 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 15.4 billion shares compared to the 17.2 billion average over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Ends Week Higher As FBM KLCI Gains 3.42 Points To 1,611.56
data.description:

The benchmark index ended at its intraday high, recovering from a low of 1,604.38 compared to its close of 1,608.14 on Oct 22, as investors remained cautious ahead of the weekend.

The FBM EMAS climbed 28.95 points or 0.24% to 11,993.45, while the F4GBM gained 2.17 points or 0.22% to 972.58.

The FBM Shariah edged up 11.59 points or 0.1% to 11,943.57, reflecting modest gains across Shariah-compliant counters.

Among the most actively traded stocks, Zetrix AI Bhd dominated trading activity, surging 2.5 sen or 50% to 7.5 sen, with approximately 392.85 million shares changing hands.

VS Industry Bhd remained unchanged at 33 sen on trading volume of 70.28 million shares, while Top Glove Corporation Bhd rose four sen to 92 sen, with 46.33 million shares traded.

Ni Hsin Group Bhd gained three sen to 49 sen on 34.08 million shares, while MAG Holdings Bhd was flat at 16 sen, with 28.89 million shares transacted.

data.title: Gold Could Slide To US$3,800 As Bearish Momentum Strengthens
data.description:
RHB Research has maintained its bearish outlook on COMEX gold futures, warning that the precious metal could fall towards US$3,800 per ounce if it breaches the crucial US$4,000 support level following a sharp sell-off on Thursday (Oct 22).

In its latest technical assessment, the research house recommended that traders maintain their short positions as gold continued to weaken, moving further away from its key moving averages.

COMEX gold closed at US$4,060.40 per ounce on Thursday, after opening at US$4,159 and briefly reaching an intraday high of US$4,164.30.

Selling pressure subsequently intensified, pushing prices to a session low of US$4,036.80 before the metal recovered slightly towards the close.

RHB said gold prices were now drifting further below both the 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages (SMA), indicating that bearish momentum remained firmly intact.

The research house expects the downward movement to continue, potentially pushing prices towards the psychological support level of US$4,000 per ounce.

A sustained break below that threshold could trigger further weakness towards the next major support level at US$3,800.

However, RHB identified US$4,200 as the immediate resistance level that could limit any short-term price recovery.

A stronger rebound would face additional resistance at US$4,300, which the research house considers an important threshold for assessing whether the current bearish trading setup remains valid.

Given the latest price movements, RHB reiterated its recommendation for traders to retain short positions initiated at US$4,284.80, based on the closing price of Sept 23.

To manage trading risks, the research house maintained its stop-loss level at US$4,300.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Slips At Midday As FBM KLCI Falls 3.05 Points, Losers Outpace Gainers

Batu Kawan Bhd lost 22 sen to RM19.08, ViTrox Corporation Bhd declined 20 sen to RM10.38, while Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd slipped 16 sen to RM19.84.

On the gainers’ list, Nestlé (M) Bhd topped the chart, advancing 54 sen to RM89.50, followed by Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd, which climbed 46 sen to RM12.74.

Kelington Group Bhd rose 16 sen to RM8.54, while Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd gained 16 sen to RM4.65. Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd added 12 sen to RM20.42.

The midday performance reflected cautious investor sentiment amid regional market weakness, although selective gains in mid-cap and heavyweight stocks helped cushion the broader decline.

data.title: Bitcoin Slides Towards US$81,000, Ethereum Falls Below US$2,400 As Crypto Selling Intensifies
data.description:
Bitcoin and Ethereum remained under pressure on Oct 23, as renewed selling across cryptocurrency markets weighed on investor sentiment amid weakness in global equities and rising geopolitical concerns.

Bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, traded around US$81,200 during the Asian session, down approximately 3.6% over 24 hours, after retreating from levels above US$84,000.

Ethereum also struggled to regain momentum, hovering around US$2,380 after falling below the key US$2,400 level. The second-largest cryptocurrency had shed about 3.4% in the previous session, reflecting broader weakness across digital assets.

The latest downturn followed a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks and renewed concerns over elevated oil prices, which dampened appetite for riskier assets.

Despite recent inflows into spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, buying interest has struggled to offset selling pressure, leaving the cryptocurrency vulnerable to further declines.

Market attention is now focused on Bitcoin’s US$80,000 support level, while Ethereum faces a key test around US$2,400. A sustained break below these levels could intensify downward pressure as investors assess global market conditions heading into the weekend.

data.title: Asian Shares Slide As AI Fears Trigger Bond Rally
data.description:
Asian shares fell on Friday as concerns over the cost of artificial intelligence (AI) investment triggered a sell-off in technology stocks, sending investors towards government bonds and reducing expectations of further US interest rate hikes.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slipped 0.3%, bringing its weekly loss to 2.7% and marking its fourth consecutive week of declines. Japan’s Nikkei fell 1.3% and was down 5% for the week, while South Korea’s KOSPI lost 1.7%, putting it on course for a 4.3% weekly decline.

Mainland Chinese blue chips dropped 1.1% to their lowest level since July 2025, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng edged up 0.1% after falling 3% on Thursday. Taiwan’s stock market was closed due to a typhoon.

The regional losses followed an overnight sell-off on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% as investors grew concerned about the funding required for AI infrastructure. Meta shares dropped nearly 8% after the company reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade, driven by AI-related spending, and announced plans to raise capital through a two-for-one split of its non-voting shares. Tesla fell 3.1% after cutting its 2026 capital spending plans.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index also tumbled 6.72%, while South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix fell 2.5% on Friday.

The sell-off fuelled demand for US Treasuries, sending the 10-year yield down more than 19 basis points overnight, its biggest daily decline since March 2023. It later steadied at 4.9591%, below the closely watched 5% level. The two-year yield fell nearly 19 basis points overnight before stabilising at 4.6566%.

Markets also pared back expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. The implied probability of a rate hike in December fell to 85%, while expectations for next year’s tightening were reduced by almost a quarter of a percentage point.

Oil prices remained elevated despite the shift towards safer assets. Brent crude hit a five-month high of US$114 a barrel as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns over further disruption to energy supplies. Gold was little changed at US$4,021.99 an ounce after falling nearly 3% overnight.

Reuters

data.title: KOSPI Sinks 3.3% After Nasdaq Sell-Off
data.description:
South Korea’s KOSPI fell 3.3% in early trading on Friday as concerns over heavy artificial intelligence (AI) spending triggered a sell-off in US technology stocks and weighed on regional markets.

The benchmark index stood at 5,353.17, while foreign investors recorded net sales of 217.7 billion won. Institutional investors and retail investors were net buyers of 209.1 billion won and 20.9 billion won, respectively.

Samsung Electronics fell 3.26% to 207,000 won, while SK Hynix declined 2.3% to 1.199 million won, tracking losses across the global semiconductor sector.

SK Hynix had also announced that it would withdraw plans for its subsidiary Solidigm to list on Nasdaq, citing capital market conditions and share price trends. The company said, “We judged that a reevaluation was necessary to determine whether the IPO is the most favorable option for SK Hynix and existing shareholders.”

Overnight, the Nasdaq Composite plunged 2.6% to 26,008.86, its steepest daily decline since June, while the S&P 500 dropped 1.21% to 7,663.43, its biggest fall since July. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index tumbled 6.72%.

Meta shares fell around 7% despite reporting revenue above market expectations, as investors questioned the scale of funding required for AI investment. AMD lost more than 8%, while Micron and Nvidia fell around 6% and 4%, respectively. AI cloud company CoreWeave also sank about 10% amid concerns over debt-funded expansion.

Investor sentiment was further pressured by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and higher oil prices. Brent crude rose 4% to US$113.17 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate gained 2.39% to US$99.47.

Demand for safe-haven US Treasuries increased, pushing yields lower. The 10-year Treasury yield fell by more than 17 basis points to 4.972%, while the two-year yield declined by more than 16 basis points to 4.659%.

The Chosun Daily

data.title: Ringgit Gains At Open As US Treasury Yields Fall
data.description:
The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Friday as the greenback weakened amid concerns over whether heavy investments in artificial intelligence (AI) companies would generate returns quickly enough.

At 8am, the local currency strengthened to 4.0785/0855 against the US dollar from Thursday’s close of 4.0815/0850.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said investor concerns over AI-related investments had intensified following a decline in equity prices.

He added that expectations of a US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike were fading, with the two-year and 10-year US Treasury yields falling by 16 and 17 basis points to 4.64% and 4.95%, respectively. The US Dollar Index also eased 0.15% to 101.625 points.

“However, there is growing concern about growth prospects, making the rate hike decision appear to be unrealistic. As such, ringgit would likely maintain its narrow range trade today as market sentiments look defensive,” he told Bernama.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the euro to 4.5765/5843 from 4.5790/5830 at Thursday’s close, but weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.6054/6100 from 2.6035/6057. It also edged lower against the British pound to 5.4664/4758 from 5.4659/4706.

Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit rose against the Thai baht to 12.0852/1124 from 12.0973/1120 and strengthened against the Indonesian rupiah to 225.8/226.3 from 225.9/226.3. It was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.42/6.43 but weakened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1941/1998 from 3.1917/1947.

data.title: HSIF Sinks 701 Points, RHB Sees Further Downside To 22,400
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its short position on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the contract fell for a third consecutive session on Thursday, shedding 701 points to close at 22,954 points and breaking below the key 23,600-point support.

The index opened at 23,636 points and rose to an intraday high of 23,747 points before heavy selling pressure dragged it to a low of 22,887 points. It later recovered 179 points in evening trading to 23,133 points.

RHB Research said the long bearish candlestick confirmed that sellers remained firmly in control. The index continued to trade below its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages, while the Relative Strength Index remained below 50%, signalling sustained bearish momentum.

The research house expects the correction to extend towards the next support at 22,400 points, followed by 22,000 points. If a technical rebound emerges after the sharp sell-off, the previous 23,600-point support is expected to act as resistance, with the next resistance level at 24,370 points.

RHB Research retained its short position initiated at the close on 17 September at 24,572 points. Following the bearish breakout, it adjusted the stop-loss level to 24,370 points while maintaining a negative trading bias.

data.title: Nasdaq Suffers Biggest Daily Drop Since June On AI Spending Doubts
data.description:
US stocks ended sharply lower on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite recording its steepest one-day percentage decline since June 5 as renewed concerns over artificial intelligence spending weighed heavily on technology shares.

The Nasdaq fell 694 points, or 2.60%, to 26,008.86, while the S&P 500 shed 93.74 points, or 1.21%, to 7,663.43. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 11.89 points, or 0.02%, to 52,867.98.

The selloff followed a series of high-profile corporate earnings reports that raised fresh questions about the scale of investment required to sustain the AI boom.

Meta Platforms shares dropped 7% despite beating analysts’ earnings expectations, after the Facebook parent reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to AI-related spending and announced plans for a two-for-one split of non-voting shares to raise capital for the technology.

Tesla fell 3.1%, despite reporting positive free cash flow for the quarter and lowering its 2026 capital expenditure forecast.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 6.7%, marking its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23. Intel, AMD, SanDisk and Marvell each lost more than 8%.

The semiconductor index has fallen more than 26% from its record closing high on June 22, although it remains up 51.5% year-to-date. The S&P 500 has gained 11.9% over the same period.

“Investors are starting to realize that there are some holes in the AI story,” said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest. “And that’s having an impact on the indices because they’re so heavily weighted toward technology.”

Elsewhere, several companies advanced after reporting results. Spotify gained 11.1% after forecasting fourth-quarter profit above market expectations, while Blackstone rose 8.4%. Lockheed Martin climbed 7% after raising its annual sales and profit forecasts, while Procter & Gamble added 5.6% despite warning of mounting cost pressures.

Investors also monitored geopolitical tensions after Iran-backed Houthis launched fresh strikes against Saudi targets, pushing crude prices to a five-month high. Higher oil prices raised concerns that inflation could remain elevated and prompt the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again before year-end.

US labour market data showed initial jobless claims remained near multi-decade lows, potentially giving the Fed greater room to focus on inflation. Financial markets were pricing in the possibility of another 25-basis-point rate increase before the end of 2026.

Reuters

data.title: IPO Debut: RedPlanet Closes ACE Market Debut 36.84% Higher At 26 Sen
data.description:
RedPlanet Bhd closed its debut trading day on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market at 26 sen on Oct 22, gaining seven sen or 36.84% from its IPO price of 19 sen, with 84.65 million shares changing hands.

The enterprise ICT solutions provider, which specialises in geospatial and intelligent rail solutions, made a strong debut following its transfer from the LEAP Market.

RedPlanet opened at 27 sen, representing a premium of eight sen or 42.11% over its IPO price, with 5.37 million shares traded at the opening bell. The stock traded between 25.5 sen and 28.5 sen in early dealings.

By midday, RedPlanet had topped Bursa Malaysia’s most active list, rising eight sen to 27 sen on trading volume of 71.97 million shares, before easing slightly to close at 26 sen.

The company’s IPO attracted strong investor interest, with its public portion oversubscribed by 85.28 times. It received 7,031 applications for 1.77 billion shares, compared with the 20.54 million shares allocated for public subscription.

The listing exercise comprised 70 million new shares and an offer for sale of 10 million existing shares through private placement, priced at 19 sen apiece.

RedPlanet entered the ACE Market following stronger financial results for the year ended June 30, 2026, with net profit increasing 21.3% to RM6.33 million from RM5.22 million a year earlier. Revenue climbed 22.3% to RM40.72 million from RM33.30 million.

Managing Director Lian Wah Seng said the IPO proceeds would strengthen the company’s project execution capabilities, support business expansion and enhance its technology-driven solutions.

He added that RedPlanet would continue building its expertise in geospatial and intelligent rail solutions while pursuing opportunities in digital infrastructure, asset management, automation and rail safety.

UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd acted as the principal advisor, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the listing.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Bucks Regional Weakness, Climbs 5.87 Points To 1,608.14
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended the trading session for Oct 22 mixed, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) gaining a mere 5.87 points, or 0.37%, to 1,608.14 as bargain hunting in selected heavyweights helped the local market outperform most regional peers.

At 5pm, the FBM KLCI closed at its intraday high of 1,608.14 compared to its previous day’s close of 1,602.27. The index moved between 1,601.76 and 1,608.14 throughout the session.

An analyst attributed the benchmark’s resilience to continued bargain hunting in selected heavyweight counters, even as most regional markets ended lower.

Broader market indices painted a mixed picture, with the FBM 70 falling 93.23 points, or 0.54%, to 17,118.37.

The F4GBM rose 1.01 points, or 0.10%, to 970.41, while the FBM Emas edged up 8.64 points, or 0.07%, to 11,964.50.

The FBM Shariah advanced 21.11 points, or 0.18%, to 11,931.98.

Zetrix AI Bhd topped the most active list, with 99.39 million shares traded, closing unchanged at five sen.

Newly listed RedPlanet Bhd followed with 84.65 million shares changing hands, surging seven sen to 26 sen.

JAKS Resources Bhd finished unchanged at 17 sen on volume of 56.12 million shares, while VS Industry Bhd declined 1.5 sen to 33 sen, recording 54.28 million shares traded.

MAG Holdings Bhd rounded out the five most active counters, edging up 0.5 sen to 16 sen on volume of 44.43 million shares.

Despite gains in the benchmark index, the FBM 70’s decline highlighted continued weakness among mid-cap counters, suggesting buying interest remained concentrated in selected stocks.

The mixed closing performance reflected cautious investor sentiment, with bargain hunting in heavyweights providing support against broader regional market weakness.
